input.question: How much have humans changed over the last 100,000-300,000 years?
input.ground_truth: I too am interested in this question! From what I've read, there are small biological adaptations that have happened in the last several thousand years but nothing that might be readily noticeable? For example, because we as a species started domesticating animals for our benefit around 8,000 years ago, that triggered an artificial selection which has resulted in most humans being able to digest lactose as adults, though some are still lactose intolerant. That's my understanding anyway. What I'm most interested in knowing though is has our species stopped evolving on a macro level because of our ability to change our environmental conditions to suit our needs through technology, or has not enough time passed in evolutionary scales for it to make a difference anyway?

messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How much have humans changed over the last 100,000-300,000 years?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big, big family tree that goes way, way back. So far back that your great, great, great… (so many greats you can’t count them!) grandparents lived a long, long time ago.

Now, think about how you and your cousins might look a little different from your grandparents. Maybe you have a different hair color, or you’re a bit taller, or you like different foods.

Over 100,000 to 300,000 years, humans have changed a little bit like that, but even more! We started as people who looked kind of like monkeys, but not exactly. Over a long, long time, our bodies and brains slowly changed. We got better at walking on two legs, our brains got bigger (so we could think of lots of new ideas!), and we learned to talk and use tools.

But even though we changed a lot, we are still very much like our old, old family members. If you could see someone from 300,000 years ago, you might think, “Wow, they look a bit different, but they’re still kind of like us!”

So, humans have changed a lot, but not so much that we wouldn’t recognize each other as family. We’re all part of the same big, big family tree!
